project.name: EndlessSketch
project.summary: Windows deep-zoom drawing application with effectively unbounded hierarchical coordinates, durable vector operations, and rebuildable PNG LOD tiles.

main_goals.goal: Maintain a data-safe, responsive drawing workflow across arbitrary practical distances and depth levels.

architecture.style: Rust desktop application with a GPU UI, normalized hierarchical camera, persistent operation log, spatial tile index, background raster cache, and verified recovery checkpoints.
layers: BigInt hierarchical coordinates and depth-normalized camera
Brush, eraser, lasso fill, eyedropper, bookmarks, and persistent undo/redo
SQLite/WAL vector source data and rotating verified backups
Spatially filtered asynchronous 512px PNG tile cache
notes: Documents use a directory-based .esketch format; PNG tiles are rebuildable and never replace vector source operations.
Content revisions are monotonic and persisted in SQLite so a stale tile cannot become current after restart.
The current local branch is test and remains six commits behind origin/test; no pull, commit, or push was performed.
Existing untracked .idea, .ess, and .esp files are user-owned and must not be changed or committed without an explicit request.

request_analysis.request: Z + mouse zoom works, but the app closed when navigating from depth 0 to -15 and back. Fix the crash and record future extreme-depth/distance optimization.
analysis: Manual testing confirmed no visible flicker, line artifacts, fill deformation, or depth visibility defects from depth -15 through +15 after the latest tile/fill fixes.

Fill rendering now uses PNG tiles as the authoritative layer, a bounded scanline fallback for nearby depths, 4x4 raster coverage for softer tile edges, and parallel tile rendering with stale-generation skipping.

Saved Fill fallback is disabled when the camera is more than six depth levels away from the operation native depth or when the projected point count is too high, preventing whole-screen black fallback artifacts and crashes at deep zoom.
Brush/Eraser live fallback uses per-segment line rendering with endpoint circles, and new drawing input rejects excessive pointer jumps to avoid accidental long straight segments.
Fast Brush/Eraser pointer jumps now split the current draft into a new stroke instead of blocking point acceptance until the cursor returns near the previous point.
Bookmark management now uses a persistent Bookmarks window instead of a transient ComboBox, so text fields remain usable while editing.
Manual validation confirms bookmark management works normally.
Fast Brush/Eraser pointer jumps now interpolate intermediate points rather than splitting the draft stroke, so quick jerks should remain visually continuous without a single huge segment.
Manual validation confirms fast Brush/Eraser jerk handling works normally. Remaining low-priority visual issue: very fast strokes can look angular.
Space + left mouse drag panning is implemented and manually confirmed working. Drawing is suppressed while this gesture is active. Z + mouse zoom remains the next separate checkpoint.
Z + left mouse drag zoom is implemented and manually confirmed working.
New crash regression: after zooming from depth 0 down to about -15 and returning toward 0, the application closed around the middle of the return path.
Backtrace captured the deep navigation close as a fatal wgpu Out of Memory during texture creation in egui_wgpu.
Cause: GPU tile textures were retained for all visited visible sets at the current content revision, not just the current visible tile set. Rapid zoom/depth navigation could exhaust GPU memory.
Tile rendering requests now use a bounded non-blocking queue, so stale generations cannot grow memory without limit. The UI retries missing tiles on later frames instead of blocking.
Additional crash mitigation: Z-drag zoom factor is clamped to 0.5..2.0 per frame so one fast mouse delta cannot skip many depth levels at once.
GPU texture retention now keeps only textures from the current visible tile set and current revision, releasing textures from previous depths/positions.
Manual validation confirms the wgpu Out of Memory crash is fixed for fast depth 0 -> -15 navigation, return navigation, and wheel zoom.
Future optimization request: after performance settings, add a dedicated fast-zoom path to reduce tile churn during rapid zoom gestures.
Future planning: after performance/quality settings, add optimization and test passes for very large depths and lateral distances from origin, including -100..+100 and -1000..+1000 style ranges.
Future low-priority items after the settings menu: configurable hotkeys and eraser fill mode.
New known rendering defect: at depth 25 and zoom around 1.x, intermittent thin vertical seams appear between large filled/tiled regions; changing zoom usually hides them.
Workflow update: future implementation should be split into smaller checkpoints and stop after each meaningful interaction change for user feedback.
